request.spec:
On the sheet a transfer brought a person to, a steward can undo it on the same sheet-today they
arrived (a button on the row; any later day, anyone else, or a person who did not arrive by transfer
is refused with an error on the row): the person is transferred back to the sheet they came from by
exactly the transfer rules and lines, and this sheet then writes PERSON_TRANSFER_UNDONE name=<name>
to=<sheet id>.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
On the sheet a transfer brought a person to, a steward can undo it on the same sheet-today they
arrived (a button on the row; any later day, anyone else, or a person who did not arrive by transfer
is refused with an error on the row): the person is transferred back to the sheet they came from by
exactly the transfer rules and lines, and this sheet then writes PERSON_TRANSFER_UNDONE name=<name>
to=<sheet id>.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Transfer undo is built, and `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec.

**What it does:** each person row now has an **Undo transfer** button (`person-transfer-undo`). When a steward presses it, the person is sent back to the sheet they came from. This reuses the existing transfer steps unchanged, so the transfer rules and audit lines are exactly the same as a normal transfer. After that, this sheet writes `PERSON_TRANSFER_UNDONE sheet=… by=… name=<name> to=<sheet id>` and then its TOTALS line.

**When it's refused:** in each of these cases an error appears on the row (`person-error`) and nothing is written to the store or the audit file:
- the user isn't a steward on this sheet
- the person didn't arrive by transfer
- the sheet's today is no longer the day they arrived

**Changes:**
- **Stored data:** a new `arrived_on` column on people (`V100__person_arrived_on.sql`). A transfer now sets it to the destination sheet's today, so the undo can check the day.
- **Server:**
  - A new `transfer-undo.POST.yml` endpoint.
  - `PrepareTransferUndo.java` makes the checks above and points the transfer back at the original sheet.
  - `AuditPersonTransferUndone.java` writes the new audit line.
  - `PersonRepository` gained a lookup for the arrival day.
- **Front end:** the new button lives in `transfer.slot.tsx`, next to the existing Transfer column.

**Decisions for you:**
- I read "anyone else" as anyone who isn't a steward on this sheet, so any steward can undo, not only the one who made the transfer. If you meant only the person who did the transfer, that needs one more check. The test passes either way.
- Sheet clones don't copy `arrived_on`, so a person copied into a clone can't have their transfer undone there.
- The button shows on every row, and pressing it on someone who never transferred gives the error. Hiding it on those rows is a small change if you'd prefer that.
